source.text: וְאַתָּ֡ה הַקְרֵ֣ב אֵלֶיךָ֩ אֶת־אַהֲרֹ֨ן אָחִ֜יךָ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֣יו אִתּ֔וֹ מִתּ֛וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְכַהֲנוֹ־לִ֑י אַהֲרֹ֕ן נָדָ֧ב וַאֲבִיה֛וּא אֶלְעָזָ֥ר וְאִיתָמָ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother and his sons with him from among [the] sons of Israel, for his serving as priest to me: Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, [the] sons of Aaron.

en.L: And you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, for him to serve as priest to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
en.B: Now bring your brother Aaron near to you, and his sons with him, out from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests: Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
en.R: Call your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar to come to you. Choose them from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.

decisions.choice: and you: God is still speaking to Moses
decisions.reason: The instructions God began giving Moses on the mountain in 25:1 continue without a break through 30:10. After the court of chapter 27, God now turns to the men who will serve in the tabernacle and what they will wear.

decisions.choice: to serve as priest to me: Aaron's priesthood, which his sons share
decisions.reason: The verb "serve as priest" has a singular subject ("for him to serve"), pointing to Aaron as the high priest. His sons are named with him, and in verse 41 the same verb is plural: "they will serve me as priests". The priesthood is Aaron's, and his sons share it.

decisions.choice: Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar: Aaron's four sons
decisions.reason: The four sons are listed in 6:23. Nadab and Abihu went up the mountain with Moses (24:1, 9); they later died for offering unauthorized fire (Leviticus 10:1-2), and Eleazar and Ithamar carried on the priesthood (Numbers 3:4).

decisions.choice: to serve me as priests
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, since Aaron and his sons are all named and all serve (verse 41). Literal keeps the singular "for him to serve as priest".

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בִגְדֵי־קֹ֖דֶשׁ לְאַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֑יךָ לְכָב֖וֹד וּלְתִפְאָֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make garments of holiness for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.

en.L: And you shall make garments of holiness for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
en.B: You are to make holy garments for your brother Aaron, to clothe him with glory and beauty.
en.R: Make special holy clothes for your brother Aaron. They will give him honor and make him look splendid.

decisions.choice: garments of holiness: clothes set apart for God's service
decisions.reason: "Holiness" marks the garments as belonging to God and reserved for the work of the sanctuary. They are worn only for that service (verses 35, 43; 29:29).

decisions.choice: for glory and for beauty: to give honor and splendor to the office
decisions.reason: "Glory" here is weight, honor and dignity; "beauty" is splendor, a thing that adorns. The garments mark the high priest's honor as the one who comes near to God for the people. The same pair is used of the sons' garments in verse 40.

decisions.choice: give him honor and make him look splendid
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two words as what the garments do for Aaron. Literal and Balanced keep "glory" and "beauty".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֗ה תְּדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־כָּל־חַכְמֵי־לֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִלֵּאתִ֖יו ר֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וְעָשׂ֞וּ אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֧י אַהֲרֹ֛ן לְקַדְּשׁ֖וֹ לְכַהֲנוֹ־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you will speak to all [the] wise of heart, whom I have filled [with] a spirit of wisdom, and they will make [the] garments of Aaron to consecrate him for his serving as priest to me.

en.L: And you, you shall speak to all [the] wise of heart, whom I have filled [with] a spirit of wisdom, and they shall make Aaron's garments, to consecrate him, for him to serve as priest to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Speak to all who are wise of heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and have them make Aaron's garments to consecrate him, so that he may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priest.
en.R: Talk to all the skilled workers. I have filled them with wisdom. Have them make the clothes for Aaron. These clothes will set him apart as holy so that he can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priest.

decisions.choice: wise of heart: skilled, able in a craft
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of understanding and skill. To be "wise of heart" is to be gifted and practiced in a craft. The same words describe the men and women who worked on the tabernacle (31:6; 35:10, 25; 36:1-2).

decisions.choice: I have filled with a spirit of wisdom: the workers' skill is God's gift
decisions.reason: God says that he himself gave the craftsmen their skill. The same is said of Bezalel, filled "with the Spirit of God, with wisdom" (31:3; 35:31). Whether "spirit" here means God's Spirit or a gift of skilled understanding, the skill comes from God.

decisions.choice: consecrate: set apart as holy for God
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to make holy, setting someone apart for God's service. The garments are part of Aaron's consecration, which is carried out in 29:1-37 and Leviticus 8.

decisions.choice: skilled workers ... set him apart as holy
decisions.reason: Readable explains "wise of heart" as skill in a craft, and "consecrate" as setting apart as holy.

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה הַבְּגָדִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲשׂ֗וּ חֹ֤שֶׁן וְאֵפוֹד֙ וּמְעִ֔יל וּכְתֹ֥נֶת תַּשְׁבֵּ֖ץ מִצְנֶ֣פֶת וְאַבְנֵ֑ט וְעָשׂ֨וּ בִגְדֵי־קֹ֜דֶשׁ לְאַהֲרֹ֥ן אָחִ֛יךָ וּלְבָנָ֖יו לְכַהֲנוֹ־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] the garments which they will make: a breastpiece and an ephod and a robe and a tunic of checkered work, a turban and a sash. And they will make garments of holiness for Aaron your brother and for his sons, for his serving as priest to me.

en.L: And these [are] the garments which they shall make: a breastpiece and an ephod and a robe and a tunic of checkered work, a turban and a sash. And they shall make garments of holiness for Aaron your brother and for his sons, for him to serve as priest to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The garments they are to make are these: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a tunic of checkered weave, a turban and a sash. They will make holy garments for your brother Aaron and for his sons, for their service to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.
en.R: Here are the clothes they must make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash. They must make these holy clothes for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.

decisions.choice: breastpiece, ephod, robe: the high priest's outer garments
decisions.reason: The three are described in turn: the ephod in verses 6-14, the breastpiece in verses 15-30, and the robe in verses 31-35. The breastpiece is named first here, perhaps because it is the most important of them.

decisions.choice: a tunic of checkered work: a long shirt woven in a pattern
decisions.reason: The tunic was a long linen garment worn next to the body. The word describing it comes from a root used of setting or weaving squares, so it was probably woven in a checkered or diamond pattern (verse 39). The exact pattern is not known.

decisions.choice: woven tunic
decisions.reason: Readable says only "woven", leaving out the uncertain pattern. Balanced has "checkered weave".

source.text: וְהֵם֙ יִקְח֣וּ אֶת־הַזָּהָ֔ב וְאֶת־הַתְּכֵ֖לֶת וְאֶת־הָֽאַרְגָּמָ֑ן וְאֶת־תּוֹלַ֥עַת הַשָּׁנִ֖י וְאֶת־הַשֵּֽׁשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they will take the gold and the violet and the purple and the scarlet of crimson and the fine linen.

en.L: And they shall take the gold and the blue [yarn] and the purple [yarn] and the scarlet [yarn] and the fine linen.
en.B: The workers are to take the gold, the blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and the fine linen.
en.R: The workers will use gold, fine linen, and blue, purple and red yarn.

decisions.choice: they will take: the skilled workers receive the people's gifts
decisions.reason: "They" are the skilled workers of verse 3. The materials come from the offering the people gave (25:2-4; 35:5-9, 21-29).

decisions.choice: blue, purple and scarlet: wool or thread dyed in costly colors
decisions.reason: The three words name dyed material, most likely wool yarn. The first is a violet-blue and the second a red-purple, both costly dyes made from sea snails. The third, literally "worm of scarlet", is a crimson dye made from an insect. The same set is used throughout the tabernacle (25:4; 26:1).

decisions.choice: yarn
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names only the colors. Balanced and Readable add "yarn"; Literal puts it in brackets. Readable says "red" for "scarlet".

source.text: וְעָשׂ֖וּ אֶת־הָאֵפֹ֑ד זָ֠הָב תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן תּוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָ֖ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will make the ephod [of] gold, violet and purple, scarlet of crimson and fine twisted linen, [the] work of a skilled designer.

en.L: And they shall make the ephod [of] gold, blue and purple [yarn], scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen, [the] work of a skilled designer.
en.B: They are to make the ephod of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled designer.
en.R: They must make the ephod, a kind of vest worn by the high priest. Skilled workers will make it from gold thread, fine linen, and blue, purple and red yarn.

decisions.choice: the ephod: a priestly garment worn over the robe
decisions.reason: From the description in verses 6-14 the ephod was a garment like an apron or vest, held up by two shoulder pieces and tied at the waist with a woven band, with the breastpiece fastened to its front. The word is kept, since it names this particular garment (1 Samuel 2:18; 2 Samuel 6:14).

decisions.choice: fine twisted linen: linen thread of several strands twisted together
decisions.reason: Fine linen was a costly white cloth made in Egypt. Twisting several threads together made a strong yarn for weaving (26:1).

decisions.choice: the work of a skilled designer: woven with a design
decisions.reason: The word describes a craftsman who designs, here a weaver who works patterns or figures into cloth (26:1, 31; 35:35).

decisions.choice: a kind of vest worn by the high priest ... gold thread
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an ephod is, and says "gold thread", since the gold was woven in (39:3).

source.text: שְׁתֵּ֧י כְתֵפֹ֣ת חֹֽבְרֹ֗ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֛וֹ אֶל־שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָ֖יו וְחֻבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Two shoulder-pieces joining will belong to it at its two ends, and it will be joined.

en.L: Two shoulder pieces joining [it] shall belong to it at its two ends, and it shall be joined together.
en.B: Two shoulder pieces are to be joined to its two ends, so that it is fastened together.
en.R: It will have two shoulder straps attached at its two ends, to hold it together.

decisions.choice: two shoulder pieces joining: straps over the shoulders that fasten the ephod
decisions.reason: The shoulder pieces ran over the priest's shoulders and joined the front and back of the ephod. On them were set the two onyx stones (verse 12).

decisions.choice: and it will be joined: so that the ephod holds together
decisions.reason: The last clause gives the result: fastened at both ends, the ephod forms one garment.

decisions.choice: shoulder straps
decisions.reason: Readable says "straps" for the shoulder pieces.

source.text: וְחֵ֤שֶׁב אֲפֻדָּתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יִהְיֶ֑ה זָהָ֗ב תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] band of its binding which [is] on it, like its work, from it it will be: gold, violet and purple and scarlet of crimson and fine twisted linen.

en.L: And the band of its fastening, which [is] upon it, shall be like its work, of one [piece] with it: gold, blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen.
en.B: The band woven to fasten it, which goes around it, must be made in the same way and form a single piece with it, of gold, blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.
en.R: The ephod will have a woven belt. It must be made in one piece with the ephod, from the same gold thread, fine linen, and blue, purple and red yarn.

decisions.choice: the band of its fastening: a woven waistband that ties the ephod on
decisions.reason: The first word is the one used for a skilled designer's work (verse 6), so the band was a woven piece. It went around the waist and held the ephod to the body (29:5; Leviticus 8:7).

decisions.choice: from it: of one piece with the ephod
decisions.reason: "From it" means that the band was not a separate belt but woven as part of the ephod, from the same materials.

decisions.choice: woven belt
decisions.reason: Readable says "belt" for the band. Literal and Balanced keep "band".

source.text: וְלָ֣קַחְתָּ֔ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֖י אַבְנֵי־שֹׁ֑הַם וּפִתַּחְתָּ֣ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁמ֖וֹת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take two stones of onyx and you will engrave on them [the] names of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And you shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel,
en.B: Take two onyx stones, and on them engrave the names of the sons of Israel,
en.R: Take two onyx stones. Carve on them the names of the sons of Jacob, who is also called Israel.

decisions.choice: onyx: a precious stone, perhaps carnelian or onyx
decisions.reason: The stone was found in Havilah (Genesis 2:12) and was given for the ephod and breastpiece (25:7). Which stone it was is not certain; onyx or carnelian are both possible. It is also the second stone of the fourth row of the breastpiece (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the names of the sons of Israel: the twelve sons of Jacob
decisions.reason: Here "the sons of Israel" are the twelve sons of Jacob, whose other name was Israel (Genesis 32:28; 35:22-26). Each son stands for the tribe that came from him (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the sons of Jacob, who is also called Israel
decisions.reason: Readable explains that Israel here is the man Jacob, so that "sons of Israel" is not read as the whole people.

source.text: שִׁשָּׁה֙ מִשְּׁמֹתָ֔ם עַ֖ל הָאֶ֣בֶן הָאֶחָ֑ת וְאֶת־שְׁמ֞וֹת הַשִּׁשָּׁ֧ה הַנּוֹתָרִ֛ים עַל־הָאֶ֥בֶן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית כְּתוֹלְדֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Six of their names on the one stone, and [the] names of the six remaining on the second stone, according to their births.

en.L: six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six remaining on the second stone, according to their births.
en.B: six of their names on the first stone and the other six names on the second, in the order they were born.
en.R: Put six names on one stone and the other six on the second stone. List them in the order the sons were born.

decisions.choice: according to their births: in order of birth
decisions.reason: The names were to be set out from the eldest, Reuben, to the youngest, Benjamin, in the order the sons were born (Genesis 29:31-30:24; 35:16-18).

decisions.choice: this verse continues the last
decisions.reason: The verse says how the names of verse 9 are shared between the two stones.

source.text: מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה חָרַשׁ֮ אֶבֶן֒ פִּתּוּחֵ֣י חֹתָ֗ם תְּפַתַּח֙ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י הָאֲבָנִ֔ים עַל־שְׁמֹ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מֻסַבֹּ֛ת מִשְׁבְּצ֥וֹת זָהָ֖ב תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] work of an engraver of stone, engravings of a seal, you will engrave the two stones with [the] names of [the] sons of Israel; set around [in] settings of gold you will make them.

en.L: [With the] work of an engraver of stone, [like the] engravings of a seal, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; mounted in settings of gold you shall make them.
en.B: Cut the names of the sons of Israel into the two stones with the skill of a stone engraver cutting a seal. Enclose the stones in settings of gold filigree.
en.R: Have a skilled stone carver cut the names into the two stones, the way he would carve a seal. Then set the stones in gold settings.

decisions.choice: engravings of a seal: letters cut into stone as on a seal
decisions.reason: A seal was a carved stone pressed into clay or wax to mark something as its owner's (Genesis 38:18; 1 Kings 21:8). Its letters were cut deep and clear. The names were to be cut the same way.

decisions.choice: settings of gold: gold mountings, probably of filigree work
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root used of weaving or setting in squares (verse 39), so the settings were probably made of woven or twisted gold wire.

decisions.choice: Have a skilled stone carver cut
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you will engrave" with "the work of an engraver of stone". Readable makes clear that a craftsman does the carving.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתָּ֞ אֶת־שְׁתֵּ֣י הָאֲבָנִ֗ים עַ֚ל כִּתְפֹ֣ת הָֽאֵפֹ֔ד אַבְנֵ֥י זִכָּרֹ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְנָשָׂא֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־שְׁמוֹתָ֜ם לִפְנֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה עַל־שְׁתֵּ֥י כְתֵפָ֖יו לְזִכָּרֹֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you will put the two stones on [the] shoulder-pieces of the ephod, stones of remembrance for [the] sons of Israel; and Aaron will bear their names before Yahweh on his two shoulders for a remembrance.

en.L: And you shall put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel; and Aaron shall bear their names before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on his two shoulders for a remembrance.
en.B: Put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel. Aaron will carry their names before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on his two shoulders, for remembrance.
en.R: Fasten the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod. They will remind {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of the tribes of Israel. Aaron will carry their names on his shoulders when he stands before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: stones of remembrance: so that Israel is remembered before God
decisions.reason: The stones carry the names "before Yahweh". In the Old Testament, for God to remember someone is for him to act on their behalf in keeping with his covenant (2:24; 6:5). The priest brings all the tribes with him into God's presence (verse 29; 30:16).

decisions.choice: Aaron will bear their names on his shoulders: he carries the tribes before God
decisions.reason: The shoulder is where a load is carried (Isaiah 9:6; 22:22). Aaron carries the names of the tribes as he goes before God, as he carries them on his heart in verse 29.

decisions.choice: remind the LORD of the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain who is reminded ("before the LORD") and that the sons stand for the tribes (verse 21).

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מִשְׁבְּצֹ֖ת זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make settings of gold,

en.L: And you shall make settings of gold,
en.B: Make settings of gold filigree,
en.R: Make gold settings,

decisions.choice: settings of gold: the settings for the two stones, or further settings for the chains
decisions.reason: These may be the settings for the onyx stones of verse 11, now given their chains, or two further gold settings to which the chains of the breastpiece are fastened (verse 25). Either way, verses 13-14 prepare the fastenings for the breastpiece described next.

decisions.choice: filigree
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Balanced names the kind of gold work. The sentence runs on into verse 14.

source.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֤י שַׁרְשְׁרֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִגְבָּלֹ֛ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה עֲבֹ֑ת וְנָתַתָּ֛ה אֶת־שַׁרְשְׁרֹ֥ת הָעֲבֹתֹ֖ת עַל־הַֽמִּשְׁבְּצֹֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and two chains of pure gold; twisted [like] cords you will make them, [the] work of cordage; and you will put the corded chains on the settings.

en.L: and two chains of pure gold; [as] twisted [cords] you shall make them, [the] work of cordage; and you shall put the corded chains on the settings.
en.B: and two chains of pure gold, braided the way cord is braided, and fasten these corded chains to the settings.
en.R: and two chains of pure gold, braided like a rope. Then attach the chains to the settings.

decisions.choice: twisted, the work of cordage: braided like rope
decisions.reason: The chains were not made of links but of gold wire twisted or braided together like a cord.

decisions.choice: the chains on the settings: fastened ready for the breastpiece
decisions.reason: The chains are attached here and put to use in verses 22-25, where they tie the breastpiece to the shoulder pieces of the ephod.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ חֹ֤שֶׁן מִשְׁפָּט֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה חֹשֵׁ֔ב כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אֵפֹ֖ד תַּעֲשֶׂ֑נּוּ זָ֠הָב תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן וְתוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָ֖ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make a breastpiece of judgment, [the] work of a skilled designer; like [the] work of [the] ephod you will make it: gold, violet and purple and scarlet of crimson and fine twisted linen you will make it.

en.L: And you shall make a breastpiece of judgment, [the] work of a skilled designer; like the work of the ephod you shall make it: [of] gold, blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen you shall make it.
en.B: Make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled designer. Make it in the same way as the ephod, of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen.
en.R: Make a breastpiece for Aaron to use when he seeks God's decisions. Skilled workers must make it the same way as the ephod, from gold thread, fine linen, and blue, purple and red yarn.

decisions.choice: breastpiece of judgment: the pouch worn over the heart that held the Urim and Thummim
decisions.reason: The breastpiece was a square pouch worn on the chest, fastened to the ephod (verses 22-28). It is called "of judgment" because it held the Urim and Thummim, by which God's decisions were sought for Israel (verse 30; Numbers 27:21).

decisions.choice: the work of a skilled designer: woven with a design, like the ephod
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, a weaver of patterned work makes it, from the same materials as the ephod.

decisions.choice: a breastpiece for Aaron to use when he seeks God's decisions
decisions.reason: Readable explains "of judgment". Literal and Balanced keep "breastpiece of judgment".

source.text: רָב֥וּעַ יִֽהְיֶ֖ה כָּפ֑וּל זֶ֥רֶת אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְזֶ֥רֶת רָחְבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Square it will be, folded double; a span its length and a span its width.

en.L: It shall be square, folded double; a span [shall be] its length and a span its width.
en.B: It is to be square and folded double, {{units:about 9 inches|a span}} long and {{units:about 9 inches|a span}} wide.
en.R: It must be square, {{units:about 9 inches|a span}} long and {{units:about 9 inches|a span}} wide, and made of cloth folded double.

decisions.choice: a span: about 9 inches, half a cubit
decisions.reason: A span was the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger with the hand spread, half a cubit, about 9 inches (23 centimeters). The breastpiece was a square about that size on each side.

decisions.choice: folded double: a doubled cloth forming a pouch
decisions.reason: The cloth was folded over to make two layers. This gave it strength to carry the stones and probably formed a pouch to hold the Urim and Thummim (verse 30).

decisions.choice: about 9 inches / a span
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with "a span" as the units setting. Literal keeps "a span".

source.text: וּמִלֵּאתָ֥ בוֹ֙ מִלֻּ֣אַת אֶ֔בֶן אַרְבָּעָ֖ה טוּרִ֣ים אָ֑בֶן ט֗וּר אֹ֤דֶם פִּטְדָה֙ וּבָרֶ֔קֶת הַטּ֖וּר הָאֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will fill in it a setting of stone, four rows of stone: a row of ruby, topaz and beryl [is] the first row;

en.L: And you shall fill in it a setting of stones, four rows of stones: a row of carnelian, topaz and beryl [shall be] the first row;
en.B: Fill it with mounted stones in four rows. In the first row are to be a carnelian, a topaz and a beryl;
en.R: Then attach four rows of precious stones to it. The first row will have a carnelian, a topaz and a beryl.

decisions.choice: the twelve stones: precious stones, several of them of uncertain identity
alternatives: second row: turquoise, lapis lazuli, diamond
decisions.reason: The twelve names in verses 17-20 are ancient words for gems, often named by color or shine rather than by mineral, and several cannot be matched with certainty to modern stones. The first, from a root meaning "red", may be carnelian, ruby or sard; the next may be topaz or chrysolite; the third, from a root meaning "to flash", may be beryl or emerald. In the second row the stone called "sapphire" was probably lapis lazuli, a blue stone with flecks of gold, and the third may be emerald, jasper or moonstone. The stones given here follow the most likely identifications; Ezekiel 28:13 and Revelation 21:19-20 list similar stones.

decisions.choice: a setting of stones: the stones were mounted on the cloth
decisions.reason: The stones were set in gold settings (verse 20) and fixed to the front of the breastpiece in four rows of three.

source.text: וְהַטּ֖וּר הַשֵּׁנִ֑י נֹ֥פֶךְ סַפִּ֖יר וְיָהֲלֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and the second row: turquoise, sapphire and emerald;

en.L: and the second row: turquoise, sapphire and emerald;
en.B: in the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire and an emerald;
en.R: The second row will have a turquoise, a sapphire and an emerald.

decisions.choice: turquoise, sapphire, emerald: identities uncertain
decisions.reason: See the note at verse 17. The "sapphire" was probably lapis lazuli, which Exodus 24:10 recalls as the blue of the pavement under God's feet; the third stone may be emerald, jasper or another stone.

source.text: וְהַטּ֖וּר הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י לֶ֥שֶׁם שְׁב֖וֹ וְאַחְלָֽמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: and the third row: jacinth, agate and amethyst;

en.L: and the third row: jacinth, agate and amethyst;
en.B: in the third row, a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
en.R: The third row will have a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst.

decisions.choice: jacinth, agate, amethyst: identities uncertain
decisions.reason: See the note at verse 17. The first may be jacinth (a reddish-orange stone) or opal; the third, from a root meaning "to dream", is probably amethyst.

source.text: וְהַטּוּר֙ הָרְבִיעִ֔י תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ וְשֹׁ֖הַם וְיָשְׁפֵ֑ה מְשֻׁבָּצִ֥ים זָהָ֛ב יִהְי֖וּ בְּמִלּוּאֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and the fourth row: chrysolite and onyx and jasper; set [in] gold they will be in their settings.

en.L: and the fourth row: chrysolite and onyx and jasper; mounted [in] gold they shall be in their settings.
en.B: and in the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx and a jasper. They are to be mounted in gold settings.
en.R: The fourth row will have a chrysolite, an onyx and a jasper. Each stone must be set in gold.

decisions.choice: chrysolite, onyx, jasper: identities uncertain
decisions.reason: See the note at verse 17. The first is named after Tarshish, a distant land of trade, and may be chrysolite, beryl or yellow jasper. The second is the stone of the shoulder pieces (verse 9).

decisions.choice: set in gold in their settings: each stone in its own gold mounting
decisions.reason: As with the onyx stones (verse 11), each gem had its own gold setting.

source.text: וְ֠הָאֲבָנִים תִּֽהְיֶ֜יןָ עַל־שְׁמֹ֧ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה עַל־שְׁמֹתָ֑ם פִּתּוּחֵ֤י חוֹתָם֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל־שְׁמ֔וֹ תִּֽהְיֶ֕יןָ לִשְׁנֵ֥י עָשָׂ֖ר שָֽׁבֶט׃

records.literal_gloss: And the stones will be according to [the] names of [the] sons of Israel, twelve, according to their names; engravings of a seal, each according to his name, they will be for [the] twelve tribes.

en.L: And the stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve, according to their names; [with the] engravings of a seal, each according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
en.B: The stones are to bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve stones for their twelve names. Cut each one like a seal with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
en.R: There will be twelve stones, one for each son of Israel. Each stone will have one son's name carved on it like a seal. They will stand for the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: the names of the sons of Israel ... the twelve tribes: each son's name stands for his tribe
decisions.reason: Each of the twelve stones carried the name of one of Jacob's sons, standing for the tribe descended from him. On the shoulders two stones carried six names each (verse 10); here each tribe has its own stone.

decisions.choice: each according to his name: one name to each stone
decisions.reason: "Each" is literally "a man", used here of each stone. Every stone has one name.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עַל־הַחֹ֛שֶׁן שַֽׁרְשֹׁ֥ת גַּבְלֻ֖ת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה עֲבֹ֑ת זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make on the breastpiece chains of twisting, [the] work of cordage, [of] pure gold.

en.L: And you shall make on the breastpiece chains of twisted [work], [the] work of cordage, [of] pure gold.
en.B: On the breastpiece make chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
en.R: For the breastpiece, make chains of pure gold, braided like a rope.

decisions.choice: chains of twisting: the corded gold chains of verse 14
decisions.reason: These are the same kind of chains as those in verse 14, perhaps the very same ones. Verses 22-28 explain how the breastpiece is fastened to the ephod: chains at the top to the shoulder pieces, and blue cord at the bottom to the band.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ עַל־הַחֹ֔שֶׁן שְׁתֵּ֖י טַבְּע֣וֹת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֗ אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ הַטַּבָּע֔וֹת עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַחֹֽשֶׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make on the breastpiece two rings of gold, and you will put the two rings on [the] two ends of the breastpiece.

en.L: And you shall make on the breastpiece two rings of gold, and you shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
en.B: Make two gold rings for the breastpiece, and put the two rings at two of its corners.
en.R: Make two gold rings for the breastpiece. Attach them to the top two corners.

decisions.choice: the two ends: the upper corners of the breastpiece
decisions.reason: The breastpiece is square. These rings take the gold chains from the shoulder pieces (verses 24-25), so they are at its two upper corners; two more rings go at the lower corners (verse 26).

decisions.choice: top
decisions.reason: Readable says which corners are meant, as verses 24-26 show.

source.text: וְנָתַתָּ֗ה אֶת־שְׁתֵּי֙ עֲבֹתֹ֣ת הַזָּהָ֔ב עַל־שְׁתֵּ֖י הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת אֶל־קְצ֖וֹת הַחֹֽשֶׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put the two cords of gold on the two rings at [the] ends of the breastpiece.

en.L: And you shall put the two gold cords on the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece.
en.B: Fasten the two gold cords to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece.
en.R: Tie the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece.

decisions.choice: the two cords of gold: the corded chains
decisions.reason: These are the corded gold chains of verses 14 and 22, here called simply "cords".

decisions.choice: chains
decisions.reason: Readable calls them "chains", as in verse 22, so the reader can follow them.

source.text: וְאֵ֨ת שְׁתֵּ֤י קְצוֹת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הָעֲבֹתֹ֔ת תִּתֵּ֖ן עַל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַֽמִּשְׁבְּצ֑וֹת וְנָתַתָּ֛ה עַל־כִּתְפ֥וֹת הָאֵפֹ֖ד אֶל־מ֥וּל פָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] two ends of the two cords you will put on the two settings, and you will put [them] on [the] shoulder-pieces of the ephod at its front.

en.L: And the two ends of the two cords you shall put on the two settings, and you shall put [them] on the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front.
en.B: Fasten the other two ends of the two cords to the two settings, and so attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
en.R: Tie the other ends of the chains to the two gold settings on the shoulder straps. This will attach the breastpiece to the front of the ephod.

decisions.choice: the two settings on the shoulder pieces: the mountings of the onyx stones
decisions.reason: The settings are those of verse 13, on the shoulder pieces where the onyx stones were set (verses 11-12). The chains run from them down to the top corners of the breastpiece.

decisions.choice: the other ends
decisions.reason: One end of each cord is already tied to the breastpiece (verse 24). Balanced and Readable say "the other" ends.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֗יתָ שְׁתֵּי֙ טַבְּע֣וֹת זָהָ֔ב וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ אֹתָ֔ם עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י קְצ֣וֹת הַחֹ֑שֶׁן עַל־שְׂפָת֕וֹ אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֶל־עֵ֥בֶר הָאֵפֹ֖ד בָּֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make two rings of gold and put them on [the] two ends of the breastpiece, on its edge which [is] toward [the] side of the ephod, inward.

en.L: And you shall make two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastpiece, on its edge which [is] toward the side of the ephod, inward.
en.B: Make two gold rings as well, and set them at the two lower ends of the breastpiece, on the edge that lies against the ephod, on the inner side.
en.R: Make two more gold rings. Attach them to the bottom two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.

decisions.choice: the two ends ... its inner edge: the lower corners, on the back
decisions.reason: These rings are at the lower corners of the breastpiece, on its inner side facing the ephod, so that they cannot be seen from the front. They will be tied to the rings of verse 27.

decisions.choice: lower / bottom
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which corners are meant, since the upper ones already have rings (verse 23).

source.text: וְעָשִׂיתָ֮ שְׁתֵּ֣י טַבְּע֣וֹת זָהָב֒ וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֡ם עַל־שְׁתֵּי֩ כִתְפ֨וֹת הָאֵפ֤וֹד מִלְּמַ֨טָּה֙ מִמּ֣וּל פָּנָ֔יו לְעֻמַּ֖ת מֶחְבַּרְתּ֑וֹ מִמַּ֕עַל לְחֵ֖שֶׁב הָאֵפֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make two rings of gold and put them on [the] two shoulder-pieces of the ephod, below, at the front of it, close to its joining, above [the] band of the ephod.

en.L: And you shall make two rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, below, at the front of it, close to its joining, above the band of the ephod.
en.B: Make yet another two gold rings. Put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod toward the bottom of its front side, close to where it is joined, above the woven band of the ephod.
en.R: Make two more gold rings and attach them to the front of the ephod, at the lower end of the shoulder straps. Put them near the seam, just above the woven belt.

decisions.choice: below, close to its joining: where the shoulder pieces meet the ephod at the waist
decisions.reason: The shoulder pieces ran down the front of the ephod. The rings were set low on them, near the seam where they joined the body of the ephod, just above the woven band, level with the lower rings of the breastpiece.

decisions.choice: yet another / more
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark that this is a third pair of rings.

source.text: וְיִרְכְּס֣וּ אֶת־הַ֠חֹשֶׁן מִֽטַּבְּעֹתָ֞יו אֶל־טַבְּעֹ֤ת הָאֵפֹד֙ בִּפְתִ֣יל תְּכֵ֔לֶת לִֽהְי֖וֹת עַל־חֵ֣שֶׁב הָאֵפ֑וֹד וְלֹֽא־יִזַּ֣ח הַחֹ֔שֶׁן מֵעַ֖ל הָאֵפֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will bind the breastpiece by its rings to [the] rings of the ephod with a cord of violet, to be on [the] band of the ephod, and not will come loose the breastpiece from on the ephod.

en.L: And they shall bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, to be upon the band of the ephod, and the breastpiece shall not come loose from upon the ephod.
en.B: Bind the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it stays on the woven band of the ephod and does not come away from it.
en.R: Use a blue cord to tie the bottom rings of the breastpiece to the rings on the ephod. Then the breastpiece will rest above the belt and will not come loose from the ephod.

decisions.choice: a cord of blue: a thread or cord of the violet-blue material
decisions.reason: The same blue cord holds the gold plate on the turban (verse 37). Numbers 15:38 commands a blue cord on the corners of every Israelite's garment.

decisions.choice: and the breastpiece will not come loose: the purpose of the fastenings
decisions.reason: Tied at the top by gold chains and at the bottom by blue cord, the breastpiece lies flat on the ephod and cannot swing free.

decisions.choice: Bind
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "they will bind", an indefinite "they" meaning the workers. Balanced and Readable make it a command, like the verses around it.

source.text: וְנָשָׂ֣א אַ֠הֲרֹן אֶת־שְׁמ֨וֹת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל בְּחֹ֧שֶׁן הַמִּשְׁפָּ֛ט עַל־לִבּ֖וֹ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ לְזִכָּרֹ֥ן לִפְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה תָּמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And Aaron will bear [the] names of [the] sons of Israel on [the] breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he goes into the holy [place], for a remembrance before Yahweh continually.

en.L: And Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgment over his heart when he goes into the holy [place], for a remembrance before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continually.
en.B: So Aaron will carry the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgment over his heart whenever he goes into the holy place, to keep them in remembrance before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at all times.
en.R: Aaron will carry the names of the tribes of Israel on the breastpiece over his heart every time he goes into the holy place. This will always remind {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of his people.

decisions.choice: Aaron will bear the names on his heart: he carries the tribes with him into God's presence
decisions.reason: The names that were on his shoulders (verse 12) are also over his heart. The high priest comes before God not for himself only but bearing all Israel, held close and cared for.

decisions.choice: the holy place: the outer room of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: "The holy" here is the holy place, the first room of the tabernacle, with the lampstand, table and altar of incense (26:33-35). Into the most holy place Aaron went once a year (Leviticus 16:2, 34).

decisions.choice: for a remembrance before Yahweh continually: as in verse 12
decisions.reason: "Continually" means every time he serves. See the note at verse 12.

source.text: וְנָתַתָּ֞ אֶל־חֹ֣שֶׁן הַמִּשְׁפָּ֗ט אֶת־הָאוּרִים֙ וְאֶת־הַתֻּמִּ֔ים וְהָיוּ֙ עַל־לֵ֣ב אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּבֹא֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְנָשָׂ֣א אַ֠הֲרֹן אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֨ט בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל עַל־לִבּ֛וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תָּמִֽיד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you will put into [the] breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they will be over [the] heart of Aaron when he goes before Yahweh; and Aaron will bear [the] judgment of [the] sons of Israel over his heart before Yahweh continually.

en.L: And you shall put into the breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be over Aaron's heart when he goes in before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel over his heart before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continually.
en.B: Put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgment, so that they are over Aaron's heart when he goes in before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So Aaron will always carry, over his heart before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the judgment of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: Put the Urim and Thummim inside the breastpiece. They were used to learn what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} decided. They will be over Aaron's heart when he goes in to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. In this way, Aaron will always carry {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s decisions for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} over his heart.

decisions.choice: the Urim and the Thummim: objects by which God's decisions were sought
decisions.reason: The Urim and Thummim were kept in the breastpiece and used to ask God for a decision, probably by giving a yes or no answer (Numbers 27:21; 1 Samuel 14:41; 28:6; Ezra 2:63). What they looked like and how they were used is not told. The names may mean "lights" and "perfections", but this is uncertain, so the words are left untranslated.

decisions.choice: the judgment of the sons of Israel: the means of deciding for the people
decisions.reason: "Judgment" here is the decision God gives for Israel in matters brought before him. With the Urim and Thummim over his heart, Aaron carries the means of seeking those decisions.

decisions.choice: Urim and Thummim
decisions.reason: The names are kept at every level, since their meaning is uncertain. Readable adds a sentence saying what they were for.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ אֶת־מְעִ֥יל הָאֵפ֖וֹד כְּלִ֥יל תְּכֵֽלֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make [the] robe of the ephod entirely [of] violet.

en.L: And you shall make the robe of the ephod entirely [of] blue.
en.B: The robe that goes under the ephod is to be made wholly of blue.
en.R: Make the robe worn under the ephod. It must be all blue.

decisions.choice: the robe of the ephod: the long robe worn under the ephod
decisions.reason: The robe was a long outer garment, worn over the tunic and under the ephod (29:5; Leviticus 8:7). It is named after the ephod because it was worn with it.

decisions.choice: entirely of blue: woven wholly of the violet-blue material
decisions.reason: Unlike the ephod, with its mix of colors, the robe was all of one color, the violet-blue of verse 5 (39:22).

decisions.choice: goes under / worn under
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the robe is worn with the ephod. Literal keeps "the robe of the ephod".

source.text: וְהָיָ֥ה פִֽי־רֹאשׁ֖וֹ בְּתוֹכ֑וֹ שָׂפָ֡ה יִֽהְיֶה֩ לְפִ֨יו סָבִ֜יב מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹרֵ֗ג כְּפִ֥י תַחְרָ֛א יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֖וֹ לֹ֥א יִקָּרֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And there will be [an] opening [for] its head in its middle; an edge will belong to its opening all around, [the] work of a weaver; like [the] opening of a coat of mail it will belong to it; not it will be torn.

en.L: And there shall be an opening [for] its head in its middle; an edge shall belong to its opening all around, [the] work of a weaver; like the opening of a coat of mail it shall belong to it; it shall not be torn.
en.B: In the middle there is to be an opening for the head. Around the opening put a hem of woven work, like the neck of a coat of armor, so that it will not rip.
en.R: Make a hole in the middle of the robe for Aaron's head. Weave a strong band around the edge of the hole, like the neck of a soldier's coat of armor, so that it will not rip.

decisions.choice: like the opening of a coat of mail: a strong, reinforced neck
alternatives: like the opening of a collar
decisions.reason: The word for the garment is rare and its meaning uncertain. It may be a coat of armor, whose neck was strongly bound, or simply a collar. Either way, the hem kept the opening from tearing.

decisions.choice: it will not be torn: so that it does not tear
decisions.reason: The words give the purpose of the woven edge. Leviticus 21:10 forbids the high priest to tear his clothes.

decisions.choice: Aaron's head ... soldier's
decisions.reason: Readable says whose head and what the coat of armor is.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עַל־שׁוּלָ֗יו רִמֹּנֵי֙ תְּכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י עַל־שׁוּלָ֖יו סָבִ֑יב וּפַעֲמֹנֵ֥י זָהָ֛ב בְּתוֹכָ֖ם סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make on its hems pomegranates of violet and purple and scarlet of crimson, on its hems all around, and bells of gold between them all around:

en.L: And you shall make on its hem pomegranates of blue and purple and scarlet [yarn], on its hem all around, and bells of gold between them all around:
en.B: Around its hem make pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, all the way around, with gold bells between them all around,
en.R: On the bottom edge of the robe, make pomegranates out of blue, purple and red yarn. Put them all around the edge, with gold bells between them.

decisions.choice: pomegranates: tassels or balls of yarn in the shape of pomegranates
decisions.reason: The pomegranate is a round fruit full of seeds, common in the land (Numbers 13:23; Deuteronomy 8:8). The ones on the robe were made of colored yarn. Pomegranates also decorated the temple pillars (1 Kings 7:18-20).

decisions.choice: bells of gold: small bells hung along the hem
decisions.reason: The bells rang as Aaron moved (verse 35).

source.text: פַּעֲמֹ֤ן זָהָב֙ וְרִמּ֔וֹן פַּֽעֲמֹ֥ן זָהָ֖ב וְרִמּ֑וֹן עַל־שׁוּלֵ֥י הַמְּעִ֖יל סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: a bell of gold and a pomegranate, a bell of gold and a pomegranate, on [the] hems of the robe all around.

en.L: a bell of gold and a pomegranate, a bell of gold and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe all around.
en.B: a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe.
en.R: The bells and pomegranates must take turns all the way around the edge of the robe.

decisions.choice: a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate: alternating
decisions.reason: The repetition pictures the pattern: bells and pomegranates set in turn all the way around the hem.

decisions.choice: take turns
decisions.reason: Readable states the pattern instead of repeating the words.

source.text: וְהָיָ֥ה עַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לְשָׁרֵ֑ת וְנִשְׁמַ֣ע ק֠וֹלוֹ בְּבֹא֨וֹ אֶל־הַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ לִפְנֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה וּבְצֵאת֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on Aaron to minister, and its sound will be heard when he goes into the holy [place] before Yahweh and when he comes out, and not he will die.

en.L: And it shall be upon Aaron to minister, and its sound shall be heard when he goes into the holy [place] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and when he comes out, and he shall not die.
en.B: The robe is to be on Aaron when he ministers. As he enters the holy place to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and as he leaves, its ringing will be heard, and so he will not die.
en.R: Aaron must wear the robe when he serves {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The bells will ring when he goes into the holy place and when he comes out. Then he will not die.

decisions.choice: its sound will be heard ... and he will not die: the priest comes before God only as God commands
decisions.reason: Coming into God's presence was dangerous for anyone who did not come in the way God set (19:21; Leviticus 10:1-2; 16:2). The text does not say why the sound of the bells kept Aaron from death. It may be that they marked his coming and going as one dressed and serving as God required, or that they announced him as he went in before God.

decisions.choice: to minister: to serve at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the service priests and Levites do in the sanctuary (verse 43; 29:30).

decisions.choice: The bells will ring
decisions.reason: Readable names what makes the sound.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ צִּ֖יץ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וּפִתַּחְתָּ֤ עָלָיו֙ פִּתּוּחֵ֣י חֹתָ֔ם קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make a plate of pure gold and you will engrave on it [with] engravings of a seal: holiness to Yahweh.

en.L: And you shall make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it [like the] engravings of a seal, 'Holiness to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'
en.B: You are to make a plate of pure gold and cut on it, the way a seal is cut, the words 'Holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'
en.R: Make a plate of pure gold. Carve these words on it, the way a seal is carved: 'Holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'

decisions.choice: a plate: a shining ornament, worn on the forehead
decisions.reason: The word is used elsewhere of a flower or blossom (Isaiah 40:7). Here it is a flat piece of gold that shone on the front of the turban. In 29:6 and 39:30 it is also called "the holy crown".

decisions.choice: Holy to Yahweh: Aaron belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The words say that the one who wears them is set apart to Yahweh. They declare the purpose of the whole priesthood. Zechariah 14:20-21 looks to a day when the same words will be written even on horses' bells and cooking pots.

decisions.choice: Holy to the LORD
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun "Holiness"; Balanced and Readable say "Holy", the natural form of an inscription.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתָּ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ עַל־פְּתִ֣יל תְּכֵ֔לֶת וְהָיָ֖ה עַל־הַמִּצְנָ֑פֶת אֶל־מ֥וּל פְּנֵֽי־הַמִּצְנֶ֖פֶת יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put it on a cord of violet, and it will be on the turban; to [the] front of [the] face of the turban it will be.

en.L: And you shall put it on a cord of blue, and it shall be on the turban; at the front of the face of the turban it shall be.
en.B: Put it on a cord of blue and set it on the turban. It belongs on the turban's front.
en.R: Tie it to the front of the turban with a blue cord.

decisions.choice: the turban: the high priest's head wrapping
decisions.reason: The turban was a length of fine linen wound around the head (verse 39). The gold plate was tied to its front, so that it rested on Aaron's forehead (verse 38).

source.text: וְהָיָה֮ עַל־מֵ֣צַח אַהֲרֹן֒ וְנָשָׂ֨א אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַקְדִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְכָֽל־מַתְּנֹ֖ת קָדְשֵׁיהֶ֑ם וְהָיָ֤ה עַל־מִצְחוֹ֙ תָּמִ֔יד לְרָצ֥וֹן לָהֶ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on [the] forehead of Aaron, and Aaron will bear the guilt of the holy things which [the] sons of Israel consecrate, for all [the] gifts of their holy things; and it will be on his forehead continually, for acceptance for them before Yahweh.

en.L: And it shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall bear the guilt of the holy things which the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel consecrate, all their holy gifts; and it shall be on his forehead continually, for acceptance for them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Aaron is to wear it on his forehead. In this way he will carry the guilt of the holy things the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} consecrate, whatever holy gifts they bring. It will rest on his forehead at all times, so that they find acceptance before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Aaron must wear it on his forehead. Then if anything is wrong with the holy gifts the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} bring, Aaron will take the blame for it. He must always wear it on his forehead so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will accept the people and their gifts.

decisions.choice: Aaron will bear the guilt of the holy things: he takes on himself any fault in the people's offerings
decisions.reason: To "bear guilt" can mean to suffer for one's own sin (verse 43) or to carry away or answer for another's (Leviticus 10:17; 16:22). Here the high priest, marked "Holy to Yahweh", answers for any fault or impurity in the gifts the people bring, so that their offerings are not rejected.

decisions.choice: for acceptance for them: so that the people are accepted
decisions.reason: "Acceptance" is God's favor toward a worshiper and his offering (Leviticus 1:3-4; 22:20-21). "Them" may be the people or their gifts; when the gifts are accepted, so are the givers.

decisions.choice: if anything is wrong with ... will take the blame for it
decisions.reason: Readable explains "bear the guilt of the holy things". Literal and Balanced keep "bear the guilt".

source.text: וְשִׁבַּצְתָּ֙ הַכְּתֹ֣נֶת שֵׁ֔שׁ וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ מִצְנֶ֣פֶת שֵׁ֑שׁ וְאַבְנֵ֥ט תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה רֹקֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will weave in checkered work the tunic [of] fine linen, and you will make a turban [of] fine linen, and a sash you will make, [the] work of an embroiderer.

en.L: And you shall weave the tunic in checkered work [of] fine linen, and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and a sash you shall make, [the] work of an embroiderer.
en.B: Weave the tunic in a checkered weave from fine linen. The turban too is to be of fine linen. For the sash, make one worked in colors by an embroiderer.
en.R: Weave the tunic from fine linen with a pattern of squares. Make the turban of fine linen too. And have a skilled worker make a sash with colorful designs.

decisions.choice: weave in checkered work: weave with a pattern
decisions.reason: See the note at verse 4. The verb is from the same root as "checkered", and probably describes a woven pattern of squares or diamonds.

decisions.choice: the work of an embroiderer: work in colored thread
decisions.reason: The word describes one who works in colors, either by embroidery or by weaving colored patterns. The sash was made of fine linen and the three colors of yarn (39:29).

source.text: וְלִבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה כֻתֳּנֹ֔ת וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם אַבְנֵטִ֑ים וּמִגְבָּעוֹת֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם לְכָב֖וֹד וּלְתִפְאָֽרֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And for [the] sons of Aaron you will make tunics, and you will make for them sashes, and headdresses you will make for them, for glory and for beauty.

en.L: And for Aaron's sons you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them, and headdresses you shall make for them, for glory and for beauty.
en.B: Aaron's sons are also to have tunics; make sashes and caps for them as well, for glory and for beauty.
en.R: Also make tunics, sashes and caps for Aaron's sons. These clothes will give them honor and make them look splendid.

decisions.choice: headdresses: caps, simpler than Aaron's turban
decisions.reason: The word for the sons' headdresses differs from the high priest's "turban" (verse 39). They were probably round caps or bands of linen (39:28).

decisions.choice: for glory and for beauty: as Aaron's garments
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 2: the sons' garments, though plainer, also give honor and splendor to their service.

decisions.choice: caps
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "caps", to set them apart from the high priest's turban. Literal has "headdresses".

source.text: וְהִלְבַּשְׁתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶת־אַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֔יךָ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וּמָשַׁחְתָּ֨ אֹתָ֜ם וּמִלֵּאתָ֧ אֶת־יָדָ֛ם וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם וְכִהֲנ֥וּ לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will clothe with them Aaron your brother and his sons with him, and you will anoint them and you will fill their hand and you will consecrate them, and they will serve as priests to me.

en.L: And you shall clothe Aaron your brother with them, and his sons with him, and you shall anoint them and fill their hand and consecrate them, and they shall serve as priests to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Clothe your brother Aaron, and his sons with him, in these garments. Then anoint them, ordain them and consecrate them to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.
en.R: Put these clothes on your brother Aaron and his sons. Then pour oil on them, give them their office, and set them apart as holy. They will serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.

decisions.choice: fill their hand: ordain, install in the priestly office
decisions.reason: To "fill the hand" of someone is to install him in an office, especially as a priest (29:9; Leviticus 8:33; Judges 17:5, 12). The ram of ordination is named after the phrase (29:22).

decisions.choice: anoint: pour oil on, to set apart for God
decisions.reason: Anointing with the holy oil marked a person or thing as set apart for God (29:7; 30:30).

decisions.choice: ordain / give them their office
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom "fill their hand"; Balanced says "ordain" and Readable explains it. Readable says "pour oil on" for "anoint".

source.text: וַעֲשֵׂ֤ה לָהֶם֙ מִכְנְסֵי־בָ֔ד לְכַסּ֖וֹת בְּשַׂ֣ר עֶרְוָ֑ה מִמָּתְנַ֥יִם וְעַד־יְרֵכַ֖יִם יִהְיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And make for them undergarments of linen to cover [the] flesh of nakedness; from [the] hips and to [the] thighs they will be.

en.L: And make for them linen undergarments to cover [the] flesh of nakedness; from [the] hips to [the] thighs they shall be.
en.B: Make them linen undergarments to cover the nakedness of their bodies; they are to reach from the hips down to the thighs.
en.R: Make linen underwear for them to cover their private parts. It must reach from the waist to the thighs.

decisions.choice: linen undergarments: short trousers of linen
decisions.reason: The garment covered the body from the hips to the thighs, like short trousers. It was made of linen, as were all the priests' garments worn in the holy place (Leviticus 16:4; Ezekiel 44:17-18).

decisions.choice: to cover the flesh of nakedness: modesty in God's service
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:26 forbade steps up to the altar, so that nakedness would not be exposed on it. The undergarments guard the priests' modesty as they serve at the altar.

decisions.choice: private parts
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "the flesh of nakedness" means.

source.text: וְהָיוּ֩ עַל־אַהֲרֹ֨ן וְעַל־בָּנָ֜יו בְּבֹאָ֣ם׀אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֗ד א֣וֹ בְגִשְׁתָּ֤ם אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לְשָׁרֵ֣ת בַּקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וְלֹא־יִשְׂא֥וּ עָוֺ֖ן וָמֵ֑תוּ חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֛ם ל֖וֹ וּלְזַרְע֥וֹ אַחֲרָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they will be on Aaron and on his sons when they go into [the] tent of meeting or when they draw near to the altar to minister in the holy [place], and not they will bear guilt and die. A statute forever [it is] for him and for his offspring after him.

en.L: And they shall be on Aaron and on his sons when they go into the tent of meeting or when they draw near to the altar to minister in the holy [place], and they shall not bear guilt and die. [It is] a statute forever for him and for his offspring after him.
en.B: These are to be on Aaron and his sons when they go into the tent of meeting, or when they come near the altar to serve in the holy place; then they will not bring guilt on themselves and die. It is a statute for all time for Aaron and for his descendants after him.
en.R: Aaron and his sons must wear them when they go into the tent of meeting, and when they come near the altar to serve in the holy place. If they do not, they will be guilty and will die. This is a rule for all time for Aaron and his descendants.

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: the tabernacle, where God meets with his people
decisions.reason: The tent of meeting is another name for the tabernacle, the place where God meets with Moses and the people (27:21; 29:42-43).

decisions.choice: to minister in the holy place: in the sanctuary area
alternatives: inside the tent, in its first room
decisions.reason: "The holy" here may be the holy place inside the tent, or the sanctuary as a whole, including the altar in the courtyard. Either way, it is the place of the priests' service.

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a lasting rule for the priestly line
decisions.reason: The rule holds for Aaron and his descendants for as long as the priesthood lasts (12:14; 27:21; 29:9).

decisions.choice: a statute forever / a statute for all time / a rule for all time
decisions.reason: As in 12:14, "statute forever" at Literal, "statute for all time" at Balanced and "rule for all time" at Readable.
